title: Etale-space realization of an arbitrary etale sheaf and pro-etale comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the small etale and pro-etale sites and comparison $
u_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Enlarge the ambient universe if necessary so that the disjoint union of a set of representable generators with sections of a given sheaf is an allowed scheme [def-weil-size-convention]. For an algebraic space $E$ over $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], say $E	o X$ is etale when the composite $V	o X$ is etale for every representable etale scheme chart $V	o E$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $h_E^{\mathrm{et}}(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,E)$ and $h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,E)$ on these two sites. The functor $E\mapsto h_E^{\mathrm{et}}$ from etale algebraic spaces over $X$ whose displayed section sets lie in the chosen sheaf universe to sheaves of sets in that universe on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an equivalence. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $
u_X^*h_E^{\mathrm{et}}\cong h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}$. For every weakly etale $u:U	o X$, the base change $E_U=E	imes_XU$ is etale over $U$ and these identifications restrict to $h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}|_U\cong
u_U^*h_{E_U}^{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0GF6 (lemma-sheaf-gives-space), construction preceding it and parts (1)-(3), with its set-theoretic condition; full faithfulness by this construction. Pro-etale realization and restriction: Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 5.1.1 and 5.4.1, pp.34,39, applied to the etale presentation of the espace etale.

proof.text: Choose the small skeleton and the larger scheme universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Index a family by all pairs $(A,a)$, with $A$ an object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $a\in\mathcal F(A)$. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] gives a map $h_A^{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal F$ for each pair. These representables are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf]. Form $V=\coprod_{(A,a)}A$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. It is etale over $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source], applied to its disjoint open summands. The sheaf axiom glues the sections $a$ over these summands into a section of $\mathcal F(V)$ and hence a map $p:h_V^{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal F$. This map is even surjective on sections: for any $a\in\mathcal F(A)$, the inclusion of the corresponding summand $A\to V$ maps to $a$. Consequently $p$ is an epimorphism (two maps out of $\mathcal F$ agreeing after $p$ agree on every section).

source.place: Tag 0GF6 (lemma-sheaf-gives-space), representable generators, size footnote and scheme coproduct; the epimorphism argument is written out.

proof.text:
Put $W=V\times_XV$, with projections $\pi_1,\pi_2$, and let $a=p_V(\mathrm{id}_V)$. The scheme-level cases of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] show that $W\to X$ is etale and that any $X$-morphism between etale $X$-schemes is etale. On $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ define $H(T\xrightarrow{g}W)$ to be a singleton if $\mathcal F(\pi_1g)(a)=\mathcal F(\pi_2g)(a)$, and empty otherwise. The composites $T\to X$ are etale, so this is defined. It is a subsheaf of the final sheaf: equality of the two sections can be checked on a covering by the separatedness axiom of $\mathcal F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-subsheaf-final-open], $H$ is represented by a unique open $R\subset W$. For an etale $X$-scheme $T$ and maps $b,c:T\to V$, the map $(b,c):T\to W$ is etale by the same permanence lemma. Applying the description of $H$ to this map gives
$$ (b,c)\text{ factors through }R\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p_T(b)=p_T(c). $$
Thus $h_R^{\mathrm{et}}=h_V^{\mathrm{et}}\times_{\mathcal F}h_V^{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, open support relation; the omitted detail is supplied using etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HV (lemma-support-subsheaf-final).

proof.text: The open subscheme $R$ is etale over $X$: its points have the same etale affine charts as the corresponding points of $W$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The projections $s,t:R\to V$ are then etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Reflexivity of equality of sections makes the diagonal $V\to W$ factor through $R$; symmetry gives the swap $R\to R$; transitivity gives $R\times_{t,V,s}R\to R$. Here each domain is etale over $X$, so the preceding kernel-pair identity and Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] produce these actual scheme morphisms, not merely identities on etale test points. Their defining projection identities imply that $R(T)$ is an equivalence relation on $V(T)$ for every $X$-scheme $T$. The open immersion $R\to W$ is a monomorphism. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer], applied to $p$, identifies $\mathcal F$ as the coequalizer of $h_R^{\mathrm{et}}\rightrightarrows h_V^{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, etale equivalence relation and coequalizer diagram; sites.tex Tag 086K (lemma-coequalizer-surjection).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] with $S=X$ to this monomorphic etale equivalence relation. It constructs the fppf sheaf quotient $E=V/R$ as an algebraic space, with a representable etale surjective atlas $q:h_V\to E$ and $h_R\cong h_V\times_Eh_V$. Its statement also supplies etale-local lifting of every section of $E$ over a scheme. At this point the conclusion is an algebraic space over $X$; etaleness of $E\to X$ and the identification of its small-etale restriction will be proved next.

source.place: Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation), including the atlas, kernel-pair and etale-local lifting clauses; used in Tag 0GF6.

proof.text: Let $B\to E$ be any representable etale map from a scheme. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], $P=B\times_EV$ is a scheme, $P\to B$ is etale and surjective, and $P\to V$ is etale. Since $V\to X$ is etale, $P\to X$ is etale by the scheme composition case of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] with its $(T,X,Y)=(X,B,P)$: its hypotheses are precisely the surjective etale map $P\to B$ and the etale composite $P\to X$. It follows that $B\to X$ is etale. Since $B\to E$ was arbitrary, this proves that the constructed $E\to X$ is etale in the chartwise sense required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03FS (lemma-etale-local), source-atlas argument written using descent.tex Tag 036W (lemma-etale-etale-local-source).

proof.text: The presheaf $h_E^{\mathrm{et}}$ is a sheaf: [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] gives descent of morphisms into $E$, and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] applies to every covering of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. By the etale-local lifting clause of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], every section of $h_E^{\mathrm{et}}$ lifts to $h_V^{\mathrm{et}}$ on an etale covering. These local lifts show that $q^{\mathrm{et}}$ is an epimorphism: equality of two maps after $q^{\mathrm{et}}$ implies equality locally on every section, hence equality by the sheaf axiom. The kernel-pair clause of that same quotient lemma restricts to $h_R^{\mathrm{et}}=h_V^{\mathrm{et}}\times_{h_E^{\mathrm{et}}}h_V^{\mathrm{et}}$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer] makes $h_E^{\mathrm{et}}$ a coequalizer of the very same pair as $\mathcal F$. The two universal properties give inverse isomorphisms $h_E^{\mathrm{et}}\cong\mathcal F$ commuting with the maps from $h_V^{\mathrm{et}}$. This proves essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, part (3); spaces.tex Tag 02WW lifting and kernel-pair clauses, and sites.tex Tag 086K. The restriction argument is explicit.

proof.text: For any etale algebraic space $E_1\to X$, choose an atlas $q_1:A\to E_1$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its kernel pair $B=A\times_{E_1}A$ is a scheme by representability of the diagonal. Both $A$ and $B$ are etale over $X$, using the chartwise hypothesis on $E_1$ and [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. For any scheme $T\to E_1$, the scheme $T\times_{E_1}A\to T$ is etale and surjective and has a tautological lift to $A$. On the small etale site of $X$ (with $T$ etale over $X$) it is an etale covering. On the big fppf site of $X$ it is an fppf covering, since an etale map is flat and locally finitely presented [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fppf-site]. On the small etale site $h_{E_1}^{\mathrm{et}}$ is a sheaf, as in Step 6, by [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]; on the big fppf site it is a sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The sheaf axiom consequently makes $h_A\to h_{E_1}$ epimorphic on either site, with kernel pair $h_B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer], $h_{E_1}$ is the coequalizer of this atlas kernel pair on both sites. The larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention] makes the sites and indexing diagrams small where needed.

source.place: Tag 086K on the small etale and big fppf sites; the atlas lifting argument uses the definitions in spaces.tex Tag 025Y. This supplies the presentation argument needed for full faithfulness.

proof.text: Given $\alpha:h_{E_1}^{\mathrm{et}}\to h_{E_2}^{\mathrm{et}}$, compose it with $h_A^{\mathrm{et}}\to h_{E_1}^{\mathrm{et}}$ from Step 7. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] identifies the result with an $X$-morphism $a:A\to E_2$. Naturality on the etale $X$-scheme $B$ gives $a\circ s=a\circ t$. The big-fppf coequalizer of Step 7, obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer], therefore extends $a$ uniquely to a map of fppf sheaves $E_1\to E_2$, hence to a morphism of algebraic spaces by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its restriction is $\alpha$ because both agree after the epimorphism $h_A^{\mathrm{et}}\to h_{E_1}^{\mathrm{et}}$. The same uniqueness proves faithfulness. Together with Step 6 this gives the asserted equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, equivalence via its presentation construction; full faithfulness is written using Yoneda and the atlas coequalizer rather than asserted as elementary.

proof.text: For any algebraic space $E$ over $X$, [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] and the covering definition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] show that $h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is a sheaf. Now take an etale $E\to X$ with the atlas $A$ and kernel pair $B$ of Step 7. For $T\to X$ weakly etale and $T\to E$, put $P=T\times_EA$. The map $P\to T$ is surjective etale by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It is weakly etale (use the etale-to-weakly-etale inclusion in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] for the base $T$); then $P\to X$ is weakly etale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. The etale cover $P\to T$ is fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], hence a covering in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its tautological lift proves that $h_A^{\mathrm{proet}}\to h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}$ is an epimorphism, by the same sheaf cancellation argument as in Step 6. Its sectionwise kernel pair is $h_B^{\mathrm{proet}}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer] presents $h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}$ as the coequalizer of $h_B^{\mathrm{proet}}\rightrightarrows h_A^{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Section 5.1, comparison on etale presentations; the fpqc sheaf input is spaces-descent.tex Tag 04P2 and the effective epimorphism input is sites.tex Tag 086K. Lemma 5.1.1 alone is not being used as an algebraic-space comparison theorem.

proof.text:
For an etale $X$-scheme $C$ and a pro-etale sheaf $G$, the adjunction and evaluation formula in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], together with [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_X^*h_C^{\mathrm{et}},G)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_C^{\mathrm{et}},
u_{X,*}G)=G(C)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_C^{\mathrm{proet}},G).$$
They identify $
u_X^*h_C^{\mathrm{et}}$ with $h_C^{\mathrm{proet}}$, naturally in $C$. Also $
u_X^*$ preserves the atlas coequalizer: maps from its image to $G$ correspond by adjunction to maps from that coequalizer to $
u_{X,*}G$, which by the defining universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] are precisely equalizing maps from the image of $h_A$. This is a direct verification of the coequalizer universal property, with no formula for values of a general $
u_X^*$ asserted.

source.place: Section 5.1, comparison adjunction. The representable and colimit computations are written out formally; Lemmas 5.1.1-5.1.2 are compatible with them but are not cited for stronger conclusions.

proof.text:
Apply Step 10 to the small-etale atlas coequalizer of Step 7. It gives $
u_X^*h_E^{\mathrm{et}}$ as the coequalizer of $h_B^{\mathrm{proet}}ightrightarrows h_A^{\mathrm{proet}}$, which by Step 9 also presents $h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore gives an isomorphism between them. More precisely, restriction gives $
u_{X,*}h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}=h_E^{\mathrm{et}}$, so the identity has an adjoint map $c_E:
u_X^*h_E^{\mathrm{et}}	o h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}$ by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. On $A$ and $B$ this is exactly the representable comparison of Step 10; hence the isomorphism just constructed is $c_E$. This description makes it independent of the atlas and natural in $E$.

source.place: Section 5.1 comparison, proved by the common atlas coequalizer; canonicity is the comparison adjunction, not an invocation of Lemma 5.1.1 for non-affine presentations.

proof.text:
Let $u:U\to X$ be weakly etale. The fibre product $E_U=E\times_XU$ exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and is chartwise etale over $U$ by the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Viewed over $U$, $E_U$ is the sheaf $(T\to U)\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_X(T,E)$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/U)_{fppf}=(\mathit{Sch}/X)_{fppf}/U$, and it is an algebraic space over $U$: for $U$-schemes $T,T'$ with maps to $E_U$, the fibre product $T\times_{E_U}T'$ is the fibre product of $T,T'$ over the algebraic space $E\times_XU$, a scheme by [def-trf-algebraic-space], with its map to $U$ through $T$, and for an atlas $A\to E$ the base change of $A\times_XU\to E_U$ along any $T\to E_U$ is $A\times_ET\to T$, so $A\times_XU\to E_U$ is a surjective etale atlas. Hence the charts of $E_U$ over $U$ are those over $X$, and the clause just cited says each composite to $U$ is etale. The slice site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ is $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$: composition with $u$ sends every weakly etale $T\to U$ to a weakly etale $T\to X$, and conversely a map $T\to U$ between weakly etale $X$-schemes is weakly etale, both by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. Coverings are the same fpqc families by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. On every object $T\to U$ of this site, the algebraic-space fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives
$$h_E^{\mathrm{proet}}|_U(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(T,E)=\operatorname{Hom}_U(T,E_U)=h_{E_U}^{\mathrm{proet}}(T).$$
Apply Steps 9-11 with base $U$ to identify the last sheaf with $\nu_U^*h_{E_U}^{\mathrm{et}}$. These are the claimed restricted identifications. They are natural in $U$: the displayed bijection sends a map $T\to E$ to its unique pair with $T\to U$, and further restriction precomposes both components; the comparison maps are the canonical adjoint maps of Step 11.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.1, p.39, functoriality by pullback on representables; the slice-site identification and fibre-product formula are written out using weakly-etale stability.
